title: Flying Home After Surgery or Treatment in Türkiye: Fit-to-Fly Rules
seoTitle: Flying After Surgery in Türkiye: Fit-to-Fly Rules
metaDescription: Fit-to-fly rules after surgery in Türkiye: airline certificates, Istanbul stay lengths, IST wheelchair and Fast Track, and DVT precautions.
quickAnswer: Airlines require a signed Fit-to-Fly certificate after recent surgery, visible bandaging, or casts, and waiting periods vary by procedure. Typical Istanbul stays run two to three days for hair transplants, five to seven days for dental or rhinoplasty, and longer for abdominal surgery. Book IST wheelchair support through your airline at least 48 hours ahead.
category: Medical Travel to Türkiye — Independent Advisory & Safety (The ITO Standard)

body.text: When do airlines require a formal Fit-to-Fly medical certificate?

Airlines can deny boarding if you have visible surgical dressings, recent stitches, or mobility limits without written clearance from your treating doctor. Under [Turkish Airlines medical fitness for flight rules](https://www.turkishairlines.com/uk-int/any-questions/medical-fitness-for-flight-guide-for-illnesses-and-other-medical-conditions/), passengers flying within defined post-operative windows must present a signed physician report stating they are medically fit to fly.

Specific waiting periods depend on the operation and carrier. For example, [Turkish Airlines guidelines](https://www.turkishairlines.com/uk-int/any-questions/medical-fitness-for-flight-guide-for-illnesses-and-other-medical-conditions/) permit travel after at least four days following stable laparoscopic surgery (with a medical report required between days five and 14) and after at least nine days following open abdominal surgery (with a report required between days 10 and 14). We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions. Always ask your clinic for a stamped, dated English certificate at your final check-up.
How many days must you stay in Istanbul after hair, dental, rhinoplasty or bariatric procedures?

Minimum recovery stays depend on swelling checks, splint or drain removal, and your surgeon's final sign-off rather than a fixed package itinerary. Booking a flexible return ticket—or adding two buffer nights—prevents costly last-minute rebooking if your clinician advises extra observation before departure.

body.text: How do you book airport wheelchair assistance and Fast Track at IST?

Istanbul Airport (IST) is one of the largest single-roof terminals in the world, and walking from check-in to distant gates can exceed 15 minutes. Wheelchair assistance is free and booked directly through your airline—such as via [Turkish Airlines Special Assistance](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-int/any-questions/special-assistance-for-passengers/)—at least 48 hours before departure, as confirmed on the [iGA Istanbul Airport Assistance Services page](https://www.istairport.com/en/flights/airport-guides/iga-cares-accessibility/accessibility/assistance-service?locale=en).

Fast Track is a separate priority lane through security and passport control. Passengers aged 65 and over receive complimentary access under the [iGA Age-Friendly Fast Track programme](https://www.istairport.com/en/services/discover/age-friendly-airport/age-friendly-airport/iga-fast-track?locale=en), while other travellers can purchase passes online or at terminal desks via [iGA PASS Fast Track](https://www.igapass.com/en/iga-fast-track-p-4000). Follow this departure checklist:

items: Request WCHR assistance 48+ hours ahead: Choose WCHR if you can climb stairs and walk to your cabin seat, or WCHS if you need help on stairs.
Carry printed clearance in hand luggage: Keep your Fit-to-Fly letter, operative summary, and prescriptions with your passport.

Arrive three hours early: Extra time prevents rushing through security, especially if travelling with a [medical travel companion](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/medical-travel-companion-turkey).
Keep prescribed medicines in original boxes: Include the Turkish pharmacy label and doctor's prescription for security screening.

body.text: What cabin precautions reduce swelling and DVT risk on long-haul flights?

Cabin pressure equals an altitude of 6,000 to 8,000 feet, and prolonged sitting increases blood-clot risk. The [CDC Yellow Book guidance on DVT and pulmonary embolism](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/travel-air-sea/deep-vein-thrombosis-and-pulmonary-embolism.html) notes that symptomatic clot risk is negligible on flights under four hours but rises measurably on longer journeys, especially after recent surgery.

Follow your surgeon's exact anticoagulation and compression-stocking instructions rather than generic internet advice. General travel-medicine guidance from the [CDC blood clots and travel resource](https://www.cdc.gov/blood-clots/risk-factors/travel.html) and [Norfolk and Norwich NHS post-surgery travel guidance](https://www.nnuh.nhs.uk/publication/download/surgery-travel-and-deep-vein-thrombosis-8/) recommends booking an aisle seat, flexing your calves and ankles every 30 minutes, standing periodically when safe, staying hydrated with water, and avoiding alcohol or sedatives. Once home, follow our [aftercare coordination checklist](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/medical-aftercare-abroad-turkey).

faq.q: Can an airline refuse boarding if I just had surgery in Türkiye?
faq.a: Yes. Gate and check-in staff can deny boarding if you appear unwell, have fresh surgical dressings, or fall inside the carrier's post-operative waiting window without a signed Fit-to-Fly certificate.

faq.q: Does a Fit-to-Fly letter need to be in English?
faq.a: Yes. Request an English-language Fit-to-Fly letter printed on hospital letterhead with the physician's name, licence number, signature, stamp, procedure date, and clearance date.

faq.q: Is wheelchair assistance at Istanbul Airport free?
faq.a: Yes. Standard PRM (Passengers with Reduced Mobility) wheelchair assistance is provided free of charge when booked through your airline at least 48 hours before departure.

faq.q: Should I book a direct flight or a layover after surgery?
faq.a: A direct flight is almost always easier after surgery because it eliminates extra terminal walks, re-screening, and prolonged sitting. If you must connect, allow at least two hours and book wheelchair assistance for every leg.

faq.q: Can I wear compression stockings on the flight home?
faq.a: Ask your operating surgeon before wearing compression stockings or taking blood-thinning medication. Properly fitted graduated stockings are commonly advised after longer procedures, but your clinical team sets the protocol.

faq.q: What if my surgeon delays my clearance to fly home?
faq.a: If your doctor advises extra recovery nights, your flexible ticket and hotel extension protect your recovery. An independent local advisor can rebook hotel rooms and airport transfers quickly without clinic sales pressure.
